utterance: Samuel, I'm sorry but you can't go back to work today. Your story and my examination strongly suggest appendicitis: an inflamed appendix. The pain moving from your belly button to the lower right, the pain with coughing and bumps, the fever, fast heart rate and the tenderness when I let go of your tummy all point that way. The urine test doesn't suggest a kidney or bladder infection. Appendicitis usually needs surgery and antibiotics, and if it's left it can burst and cause a serious infection through the belly. So I've phoned the emergency department and I'm writing a letter. Please have your mate drive you straight there now, no stops. Don't eat or drink anything from now on, in case you need an operation, and don't take more painkillers by mouth; the hospital will give you pain relief through a drip. If on the way the pain suddenly gets much worse or spreads across your whole tummy, you feel faint, very shivery or confused, or you keep vomiting, have your mate call 000 for an ambulance. I'll give you a medical certificate for work. Any questions?
reply: Surgery? Are you serious? I just wanted to get this sorted so I could get back on the tools.

utterance: I understand it's a shock. Most people have a keyhole operation, stay a day or two, and are back at light duties within a couple of weeks; heavy lifting usually a few weeks after that. The hospital team will confirm the diagnosis with blood tests and possibly a scan before deciding. Getting it treated today is the quickest way back on the tools; waiting risks it bursting, which means a much longer recovery. Please head straight there now.
reply: Alright. My mate is outside, so I will go now.
